data.name: About.Description.P01
data.value: ChronoRover is a precise time signal generator that emulates official long-wave time broadcasts to synchronize radio-controlled watches with atomic accuracy using your phone’s speaker or headphones.

data.name: About.Description.P02
data.value: Among the currently supported signals are: DCF77 (Germany), MSF (United Kingdom), WWVB (United States), JJY (Japan), and BPC (China).

data.name: About.Description.P03
data.value: Whether you’re a watch enthusiast, collector, or simply want the most accurate time possible, ChronoRover turns your smartphone into a portable time signal transmitter.

data.name: About.Description.P04
data.value: Perfect solution for Casio and Citizen owners who live beyond the range of any official time signal transmission station!

data.name: Manual.Caution.P01
data.value: This application generates loud, high-pitched noises that may cause discomfort or potential hearing damage! Leave the room while transmission is active.

data.name: Manual.Synchronisation.P02
data.value: Select the correct signal type (e.g. DCF77).

data.name: Manual.Synchronisation.P06
data.value: Manually turn on the wave reception mode on your watch, per its manual.

data.name: Manual.Synchronisation.P08
data.value: Place it immediately adjacent to an external speaker or connected headphones for best results. The built-in speaker is an alternative, though far less reliable due to lower power.

data.name: Manual.Synchronisation.P10
data.value: button above to see images of the correct watch position.

data.name: Manual.Synchronisation.P16
data.value: Upon sync completion, press the Stop button.

data.name: Manual.Troubleshooting.P02
data.value: Confirm the selected signal type aligns with your watch's capabilities.

data.name: Manual.Troubleshooting.P03
data.value: On some watches (like Casio or Citizen), the receivable signal type depends on the set home city. For example, if your watch's home city is set to BER, choose DCF77.

data.name: Manual.Troubleshooting.P05
data.value: Make sure the volume is high enough. Keep the watch as close to the speaker as possible. Try using external speaker or a headset if you are not, if you are try different one.

data.name: Manual.Troubleshooting.P07
data.value: Background noise, music, or other sounds may interfere with the time signal and cause synchronization to fail. For optimal results, use the application in a quiet room.

data.name: Manual.Troubleshooting.P09
data.value: Your watch may be a few hundred milliseconds slow after synchronization. This can occasionally be caused by the headset you are using. Try another one!

data.name: Manual.Troubleshooting.P10
data.value: During our testing, the simplest and cheapest cable models delivered the best (and perfect) accuracy.
